proxy.dialog.intro: You can send everything from this device through a SOCKS5 proxy of your choice, for every server you've joined: messages, files, calls, link previews, updates and plugins. Your servers and their media servers will see the proxy's address instead of yours. The proxy can see which servers you connect to, when, and how much you send, but not what you send, since that stays encrypted.
proxy.dialog.title: Proxy
proxy.dialog.tooLong: SOCKS5 usernames and passwords can be at most 255 bytes each.
proxy.dialog.warning: If the proxy can't be reached, Zuna won't connect at all. It never bypasses the proxy. SOCKS5 itself isn't encrypted, so the proxy's password and your servers' names travel to the proxy unencrypted. That isn't a concern for a proxy running on this computer, such as Tor or ssh -D.
proxy.dialog.warningNoWatch: If the proxy can't be reached, Zuna won't connect at all. It never bypasses the proxy. settings.privacy.keepMetadataMessage:
Photos and videos from phones usually record where they were taken, to within a few meters, and when. With this off, everyone in a chat you send them to can see that, along with the camera or phone and its serial number, the software used, and how it was edited. So can anyone they forward the files to.

Your server still can't see any of it, since files are encrypted. This only applies to this device, and to files you send from now on.
